claims.claim: 15,841 positive results not included in reported daily cases, 25 September to 2 October (PHE)
claims.passage: After rapid investigation, 15,841 cases were identified between 25 September and 2 October
claims.notes: PHE statement (live fetch, summarised by fetcher) and DHSC weekly statistics give the same figure and date range.

claims.claim: 11,968, over 75%, due between 30 September and 2 October
claims.passage: Of these, over 75% (11,968) relate to cases that should have been reported between 30 September and 2 October.
claims.notes: Matches the PHE statement as returned by the fetcher.

claims.claim: Identified overnight on Friday 2 October; data load process that transfers COVID-19 positive lab results into reporting dashboards
claims.passage: A technical issue was identified overnight on Friday 2 October in the data load process that transfers COVID-19 positive lab results into reporting dashboards.
claims.notes: Quoted phrase present verbatim.

claims.claim: "some files containing positive test results exceeded the maximum file size"; mitigation "splits large files"
claims.passage: some files containing positive test results exceeded the maximum file size
claims.notes: Fetcher quoted both phrases; 'splits large files' also appears in the Harding reply extract.

claims.claim: All outstanding cases transferred to contact tracing "by 1am on 3 October"; everyone affected received result as normal
claims.passage: All outstanding cases were immediately transferred to the contact tracing system by 1am on 3 October.
claims.notes: Also 'Every one of these cases received their COVID-19 test result as normal'; exhibit's quoted fragment is a verbatim substring.

claims.claim: The PHE statement does not use the words Excel, XLS, rows or columns
claims.passage: No, none of the words Excel, XLS, rows, or columns appear in the content.
claims.notes: Confirmed by targeted fetch of the page; the passage is the fetcher's report, not page text.

claims.claim: PHE statement published 4 Oct 2020, updated 5 Oct 2020, Michael Brodie, Interim Chief Executive
claims.passage: a news story published 4 October 2020 and last updated 5 October 2020. Interim Chief Executive Michael Brodie and Joint Medical Advisor Susan Hopkins issued statements.
claims.notes: Fetcher summary, consistent with the exhibit.

claims.claim: Health Secretary: 15,841 over the previous 8 days; failure in the automated transfer of files
claims.passage: Public Health England identified that over the previous eight days, 15,841 positive test results were not included in the reported daily cases. This was due to a failure in the automated transfer of files from the labs to PHE’s data systems.
claims.notes: Verified from local extract, not a live fetch.

claims.claim: 6,500 hours of extra contact tracing; 51% contacted a second time as of 9am
claims.passage: We brought in 6,500 hours of extra contact tracing over the weekend. I can report to the House that, as of 9 am today, 51% of the cases have now been contacted a second time for contact tracing purposes.
claims.notes: Verified from local extract.

claims.claim: "This incident should never have happened"
claims.passage: This incident should never have happened, but the team have acted swiftly to minimise its impact.
claims.notes: Verbatim; Health Secretary's own statement, framed as reported speech and not an accusation.

claims.claim: Problem "emerged in a PHE legacy system"; decision in July to replace; contracts "awarded in August"
claims.passage: The problem emerged in a PHE legacy system. We had already decided in July to replace this system, and I commissioned a new data system to replace the legacy one. Contracts were awarded in August
claims.notes: Verbatim in extract.

claims.claim: "a maximum file size error" spoken by the Health Secretary
claims.passage: However, the challenge of a maximum file size error is that it would not necessarily have appeared on that sort of flow chart
claims.notes: Phrase present in a later reply by the Health Secretary (contribution 61); extract does not show the speaker header adjacent, attribution inferred from context and exhibit's earlier statement.

claims.claim: Health Secretary said "Excel" 0 times; the word appears only in questions from Ashworth and Coyle
claims.passage: Can the Secretary of State confirm that the data could not be handed over to PHE because of the size of the Excel spreadsheet files? ... Why are critical databases in a national pandemic being hosted on Excel spreadsheets?
claims.notes: Case-insensitive search found 3 'Excel' hits as a word (2 in Ashworth contribution 6, 1 in Coyle contribution 101: 'problems with Excel spreadsheets'); other hits are 'excellent'/'Excellence'; Health Secretary never says Excel or spreadsheet.

claims.claim: Quoted Ashworth question: "Why are critical databases in a national pandemic being hosted on Excel spreadsheets?"
claims.passage: Why are critical databases in a national pandemic being hosted on Excel spreadsheets?
claims.notes: Verbatim, speaker Jonathan Ashworth (Leicester South).

claims.claim: Clark letter, 8 Oct: Secretary of State told the House issue related to PHE legacy system "which included the use of Microsoft Excel"
claims.passage: The Secretary of State for Health and Social Care told the House on Monday 5 October that the issue was related to a Public Health England (PHE) legacy system, which included the use of Microsoft Excel.
claims.notes: Verbatim from local extract; Hansard shows no such statement, which is the exhibit's gap.

claims.claim: "It is reported that PHE developers used an old format of the software, XLS, which had a set number of rows to log data that was incompatible with the volume of data being generated."
claims.passage: It is reported that PHE developers used an old format of the software, XLS, which had a set number of rows to log data that was incompatible with the volume of data being generated.
claims.notes: Verbatim; exhibit presents it only as reported.

claims.claim: Letter asks about certification of "the Microsoft Excel-based system"
claims.passage: What certification took place of the Microsoft Excel-based system
claims.notes: Verbatim.

claims.claim: Harding: "The technical issue was not caused by the use of an old format."
claims.source: Baroness Harding, National Institute for Health Protection
claims.passage: The technical issue was not caused by the use of an old format.
claims.notes: Verbatim; reply dated 12 October 2020, 4 days after 8 October.

claims.claim: Excel files "exceeded their file size threshold and so were not uploaded" as Pillar 2 volumes rose
claims.source: Baroness Harding, National Institute for Health Protection
claims.passage: Increased testing volumes from Pillar 2 meant that some Excel files used in the transfer process exceeded their file size threshold and so were not uploaded.
claims.notes: Verbatim.

claims.claim: Reply dates cases 24 September to 1 October; 6,000 hours of extra contact tracing; "(75% / 11,968)"
claims.source: Baroness Harding, National Institute for Health Protection
claims.passage: The delayed reports are all positive cases identified via Pillar 2 testing between 24 September and 1 October. ... (75% / 11,968) ... we brought in 6,000 hours of extra contact tracing
claims.notes: Verbatim from local extract; 1 day earlier than PHE is correct arithmetic; 6,500 vs 6,000 correct.

claims.claim: "As of the morning of 12 October, 79% of people testing positive have been reached and asked for details of their contacts."
claims.source: Baroness Harding, National Institute for Health Protection
claims.passage: As of the morning of 12 October, 79% of people testing positive have been reached and asked for details of their contacts.
claims.notes: Verbatim; exhibit declines to tie it to the 15,841 only.

claims.claim: "A full wash-up of the incident is ongoing"
claims.source: Baroness Harding, National Institute for Health Protection
claims.passage: A full wash-up of the incident is ongoing.
claims.notes: Verbatim.

claims.claim: Reply "splits large files" mitigation
claims.source: Baroness Harding, National Institute for Health Protection
claims.passage: A rapid mitigation has been put in place by PHE working together with NHS Test and Trace that splits large files
claims.notes: Verbatim.

claims.passage: After rapid investigation, 15,841 cases were identified between 25 September and 2 October

claims.claim: Wash-up: "this site found none published" / "No published wash-up of the incident was found"
claims.source: Baroness Harding, National Institute for Health Protection
